question: todo.md Step 4 names the bidirectional GNN-LLM loop as the core novelty. With --no-output-fusion the LLM reaches the loop ONLY through the attention bias on the flagged top-k edges. Can any in-architecture setting make that path beat not having it?
verdict: NO. The attention-feedback mechanism is inert on this graph.

protocol.control: head_only mode: the SAME loop model with the semantic signal structurally absent, so no bias is ever computed. This is the correct control. The bare GNN rung (0.5496) is a DIFFERENT model trained by a different driver; scoring against it confounds 'does feedback help' with 'is this a different network', and would have made strength50 (0.5572) look like a win when it is a 0.0021 loss.

mechanism_diagnostics.note: Measured on the trained bias module at the end of each fold. GATv2 attention logits sit on a ~1 nat scale, so a bias much below 1 cannot reorder the attention softmax.

findings: CHURN IS EXACTLY 0.0000 IN EVERY FOLD OF EVERY CONFIGURATION. The biased pass reproduces the unbiased pass prediction for prediction: identical per-class F1, identical mean entropy to 7 decimals. The LLM's judgment flips zero predictions.

Because churn is 0, the loop always trips its convergence check at iteration 2. 'Repeats until convergence' means 'stops after one inert pass'. Raising --max-iterations to 6 or 10 changes nothing, because zero times more rounds is zero.

Under the default config the learned bias is ~0.05 nats against ~1 nat attention logits, and the projection weights are still at their zero initialisation after 300 epochs (|w| 0.005-0.047). The learned strength moves from 1.5 to 1.5.

ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE ZERO INIT. Starting the projection live (--bias-init xavier, |w|=0.485) lets training drive it back down to 0.025-0.037 nats. The optimiser is actively switching the mechanism off because the bias does not reduce the loss.

NOR IS IT MAGNITUDE. --bias-init xavier --bias-strength 50 reaches a bias of 1.03-1.46 nats, genuinely the same scale as the attention logits, and churn is STILL 0.0000. A full-scale nudge reorders attention without changing a single classification.

NO CONFIGURATION BEATS THE CONTROL. Every variant lands at or below no-feedback (0.5580 +/- 0.0028). Best case is 'harmless' (strength50, -0.0021); the shipped default costs -0.0122 while informing nothing.

FEEDBACK ADDS NOISE, NOT SIGNAL. Seed sd is 0.0028 without feedback and 0.0077-0.0211 with it. The one-factor sweep's apparent winner (iters6, 0.5604 at seed 42) scores 0.5450 at seed 1, below the baseline it 'beat'. Single-seed rankings here are noise.
consequences: todo.md Step 4's central claim -- bidirectional iterative GNN-LLM interaction -- is not supported on this data. The mechanism does not run.
The loop's headline UNSW result (0.7764) comes entirely from all-edge output fusion, which is ordinary late fusion and is not the claimed novelty.

AGAF (Step 3, parallel dual-encoder) remains defensible: on ToN it is the top rung and is significantly above both unimodal baselines (+0.114 vs GNN, +0.162 vs LLM, both CIs exclude zero). That is a real result, but it is Step 3's, not Step 4's.
